title: Episode 240: Thrust, Rust vs C++, Python & More (Part 2)

sentences.en: This is such a C++ programmer thing to worry about.
sentences.zh: 这真是个典型的 C++ 程序员会担心的问题。

sentences.en: Because I used to worry about what to name things.
sentences.zh: 因为我以前总是纠结该给事物起什么名字。

sentences.en: Because in C++, C++ is a very paranoid language.
sentences.zh: 因为在 C++ 中，C++ 是一门非常偏执的语言。

sentences.en: Because you have to think about all the things that can go wrong on any given line of code.
sentences.zh: 因为你必须考虑到代码中每一行可能出错的所有情况。

sentences.en: Like you could call the wrong function, or the type the thing gets instantiated with is, we'll be missing something, or we'll have the wrong thing in it.
sentences.zh: 比如你可能会调用错误的函数，或者实例化对象的类型不对，或者我们漏掉了什么，又或者里面装了错误的东西。

sentences.en: And so you have to take this very defensive stance when writing any C++ code.
sentences.zh: 所以你在编写任何 C++ 代码时都必须采取这种非常防御性的姿态。

sentences.en: Now that I've been using Rust for a while now, I don't worry about these things at all.
sentences.zh: 现在我使用 Rust 已经有一段时间了，我完全不用担心这些问题。

sentences.en: I don't worry about what to call things.
sentences.zh: 我不用担心该给事物起什么名字。

sentences.en: I don't worry about how the code looks, because I can be confident that it works.
sentences.zh: 我不用担心代码看起来怎么样，因为我可以确信它能正常工作。

sentences.en: These problems just don't exist in Rust, I guess is what I'm saying.
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，这些问题在 Rust 中根本不存在。

sentences.en: Welcome to ADSP, the podcast, episode 240, recorded on May 21st, 2025.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到 ADSP 播客，第 240 期，录制于 2025 年 5 月 21 日。

sentences.en: My name is Connor, and today with my co-host Bryce, we interview Jared Hobrock.
sentences.zh: 我是 Connor，今天和我的联合主持人 Bryce 一起采访 Jared Hobrock。

sentences.en: This is part two of a four-part interview.
sentences.zh: 这是四部分访谈中的第二部分。

sentences.en: In this episode, we continue our conversation about Thrust, Rust versus C++, Python, NumPy, Numba, and more.
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，我们将继续讨论 Thrust、Rust 与 C++、Python、NumPy、Numba 等话题。

sentences.en: I believe Bryce and I have a ton more questions to ask you on the roots of ThruSt.
sentences.zh: 我相信 Bryce 和我还有很多关于 Thrust 起源的问题要问你。

sentences.en: I mean, I've been holding on to this question for a long time.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这个问题我憋了很久了。

sentences.en: The last time I was in New York, which was in April, we're recording this tail end of May.
sentences.zh: 我上次去纽约是在四月，我们现在录制的时间是五月底。

sentences.en: We got into a discussion of the different names for the OG name is IOTA from the, I guess technically it was the C++11 standard, but it comes from APL.
sentences.zh: 我们讨论过不同的命名，最初的名字是 IOTA，我想从技术上讲它来自 C++11 标准，但它源于 APL。

sentences.en: Well, IOTA is an integer sequence where you increment by one, one, two, three, four, five, six.
sentences.zh: 嗯，IOTA 是一个整数序列，你每次加一，一、二、三、四、五、六。

sentences.en: In Thrust, there are two different names for this.
sentences.zh: 在 Thrust 中，对此有两个不同的名称。

sentences.en: There is the counting iterator, and there is also the Thrust sequence.
sentences.zh: 一个是计数迭代器（counting iterator），另一个是 Thrust 序列（Thrust sequence）。

sentences.en: And this has been up for much debate between Bryce and I of what is the correct name.
sentences.zh: 关于哪个名字才是正确的，Bryce 和我之间一直争论不休。

sentences.en: But our first question is, do you recall, Jared, where the names for both Thrust sequence as an algorithm and Thrust counting iterator as a fancy iterator,
sentences.zh: 但我们的第一个问题是，Jared，你还记得 Thrust sequence 作为一种算法，以及 Thrust counting iterator 作为一种花式迭代器，这两个名字是从哪里来的吗？

sentences.en: do you recall where those came from?
sentences.zh: 你还记得它们的出处吗？

sentences.en: Sequence in particular, because it stands out.
sentences.zh: 特别是 Sequence，因为它很显眼。

sentences.en: I think we were aware of IOTA, and just, like, we couldn't name it, we couldn't give it that name.
sentences.zh: 我想我们当时知道 IOTA，只是，我们不能给它起那个名字。

sentences.en: That is ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 那太荒谬了。

sentences.en: We were going to, you know, it's going to be used in every example.
sentences.zh: 我们打算，你知道的，它会被用在每一个示例中。

sentences.en: We can't use a stupid name that doesn't mean anything.
sentences.zh: 我们不能用一个毫无意义的蠢名字。

sentences.en: So I think that's where sequence came from.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这就是 Sequence 的由来。

sentences.en: And maybe we sort of justified it by saying, well, the interface isn't exactly the same, so we have to change the name.
sentences.zh: 也许我们当时通过说“嗯，接口并不完全一样，所以我们必须改名”来为自己辩解。

sentences.en: We can't use IOTA.
sentences.zh: 我们不能用 IOTA。

sentences.en: And counting iterator, I think, just came straight from BooSt.
sentences.zh: 而 Counting iterator，我想是直接来自 Boost。

sentences.en: I think Boost was a, I think there was a Boost counting iterator that we just took.
sentences.zh: 我想 Boost 有一个 Boost counting iterator，我们直接拿来用了。

sentences.en: If you want to talk about names, I can tell you the story of how Thrust got its name.
sentences.zh: 如果你想聊聊名字，我可以告诉你 Thrust 是怎么得名的故事。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 好啊。

sentences.en: Ooh, I would love that story.
sentences.zh: 噢，我很想听听这个故事。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 好。

sentences.en: So, I think when I was working on it in grad school, maybe its name was STD CUDA, like, stood CUDA, just as, like, a, I don't know, a placeholder name.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想我在读研时开发它的时候，它的名字可能是 STD CUDA，就像“标准 CUDA”一样，我不知道，只是一个占位符名称。

sentences.en: When I got to NVIDIA, you know, maybe someone made the comment, it's not standard and it's not CUDA, so this is not a good name.
sentences.zh: 当我到了 NVIDIA，你知道，也许有人评论说，它既不是标准的，也不是 CUDA，所以这不是个好名字。

sentences.en: So we said, okay, fine.
sentences.zh: 所以我们说，好吧，行。

sentences.en: And Nathan had just gotten back from a tour of Asia.
sentences.zh: 当时 Nathan 刚从亚洲巡回回来。

sentences.en: So he had spent a few weeks touring Asia and touring, like, post-Soviet communist countries.
sentences.zh: 他花了几个星期在亚洲旅游，还去了前苏联的共产主义国家。

sentences.en: And he had this picture of, you know, a Soviet worker from a mural or something like that.
sentences.zh: 他有一张照片，你知道，是壁画里的苏联工人什么的。

sentences.en: And I don't know, for some reason it appealed to him.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，出于某种原因，这吸引了他。

sentences.en: And he decided, we've got to call this library Comrade, with a K, K-O-M-R-A-D-E.
sentences.zh: 他决定，我们必须把这个库叫 Comrade（同志），用 K 开头，K-O-M-R-A-D-E。

sentences.en: And we're going to use this picture I took as the avatar when we release it.
sentences.zh: 而且我们发布的时候要用我拍的这张照片作为头像。

sentences.en: I didn't really have a strong opinion about it.
sentences.zh: 我当时对这个没什么强烈的意见。

sentences.en: And I believe the – so for some reason he wanted to give the library a communist theme.
sentences.zh: 我相信——出于某种原因，他想给这个库一个共产主义主题。

sentences.en: And he's not, like, a left-wing or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 而且他并不是什么左翼分子之类的。

sentences.en: He just thought it was funny.
sentences.zh: 他只是觉得这很有趣。

sentences.en: And I remember the – so we released it on Google Code under the name Comrade.
sentences.zh: 我记得——所以我们在 Google Code 上以 Comrade 的名字发布了它。

sentences.en: And the tagline was, own the means of computation.
sentences.zh: 标语是：掌握计算工具（Own the means of computation）。

sentences.en: And we're really proud of ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们当时真的很为自己骄傲。

sentences.en: We just released this library that we were really proud of.
sentences.zh: 我们刚刚发布了这个让我们引以为傲的库。

sentences.en: We gave it a hilarious name, or so we thought.
sentences.zh: 我们给它起了一个搞笑的名字，或者我们自以为是这样。

sentences.en: And then, like, the next day, after announcing that we'd released this library, you know, to some mailing list at work,
sentences.zh: 然后，第二天，在向公司内部的某个邮件列表宣布我们发布了这个库之后，

sentences.en: we get a response from someone who was very important and influential at the time at NVIDIA, saying that, you know, communism isn't cute.
sentences.zh: 我们收到了一位当时在 NVIDIA 非常重要且有影响力的人的回信，说共产主义并不可爱。

sentences.en: It isn't funny.
sentences.zh: 这并不好笑。

sentences.en: You can't name it this.
sentences.zh: 你们不能给它起这个名字。

sentences.en: And so we were sort of shitting our pants because this guy is very important.
sentences.zh: 所以我们当时吓坏了，因为这家伙非常重要。

sentences.en: And so we couldn't – we had to, you know, save face somehow and think about a different name.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不能——我们必须以某种方式挽回面子，想一个不同的名字。

sentences.en: So it was my task to come up with a new name after Nathan had failed and, you know, gotten us in trouble.
sentences.zh: 所以我的任务是在 Nathan 失败并让我们惹上麻烦后想出一个新名字。

sentences.en: So what I did was I looked through every English word between four and six letters ending in St.
sentences.zh: 所以我做的是查看了所有四个到六个字母且以 St 结尾的英文单词。

sentences.en: You know, since we were stealing everything else from Boost, we thought we would steal the name as well.
sentences.zh: 你知道，既然我们从 Boost 那里偷了其他所有东西，我们想连名字也一起偷过来。

sentences.en: So I saw Thrust, and I said, how about Thrust?
sentences.zh: 所以我看到了 Thrust，我说，Thrust 怎么样？

sentences.en: And, you know, originally I think people were like, you know, we were going from this, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，起初我想人们觉得，你知道，我们是从这个，你知道，

sentences.en: left-wing tinge name to some sort of sexual innuendo for a name.
sentences.zh: 带有左翼色彩的名字变成了一个带有某种性暗示的名字。

sentences.en: But we stuck with it, and somehow the name was stuck.
sentences.zh: 但我们坚持了下来，不知何故这个名字就固定下来了。

sentences.en: And now it's, you know, it's just firmly – firmly means this library's name and nothing else.
sentences.zh: 现在它，你知道，它已经牢牢地——牢牢地代表了这个库的名字，别无他意。

sentences.en: But that's where the name came from.
sentences.zh: 但这就是名字的由来。

sentences.en: Just another thing we stole from BooSt.
sentences.zh: 只是我们从 Boost 那里偷来的另一件事。

sentences.en: I was going to say is I always thought that Thrust and Boost, like, they share the same one-syllable ST ending, and that was intentional.
sentences.zh: 我正想说，我一直认为 Thrust 和 Boost，它们共享同一个单音节的 ST 结尾，这是故意的。

sentences.en: And it turns out that is the case.
sentences.zh: 结果确实如此。

sentences.en: I had no idea.
sentences.zh: 我完全不知道。

sentences.en: I had no idea that that was intentional.
sentences.zh: 我完全不知道那是故意的。

sentences.en: I knew about the Comrade thing.
sentences.zh: 我知道 Comrade 的事。

sentences.en: There was a guy wearing the Thrust t-shirt, which we haven't mentioned until now.
sentences.zh: 有一个人穿着 Thrust 的 T 恤，我们直到现在才提到它。

sentences.en: At one point, Bryce left the Microsoft Teams meeting to go and disappear, and he came back with a Thrust t-shirt.
sentences.zh: 有一次，Bryce 离开了 Microsoft Teams 会议消失了，回来时穿了一件 Thrust T 恤。

sentences.en: So I had – I should not say this for a variety of reasons, but I had these t-shirts made, like, right when I first started NVIDIA.
sentences.zh: 所以我不得不——出于各种原因我不该说这个，但我刚开始在 NVIDIA 工作时就做了这些 T 恤。

sentences.en: And I believe that the only other person who has a Thrust t-shirt is Jared, because I think I gave you one at, like, a committee meeting in 2018 or something.
sentences.zh: 我相信唯一还有 Thrust T 恤的人是 Jared，因为我想我在 2018 年左右的委员会会议上给了你一件。

sentences.en: But I had, like, five of them made, and I think, like, one of them got, like, faded in the wash, and so I tossed it.
sentences.zh: 但我当时做了五件，我想其中一件在洗涤时褪色了，所以我就扔了。

sentences.en: And I think I gave one to Jared, and I guess I must have misplaced one, because this is the only one that I have left.
sentences.zh: 我想我给了 Jared 一件，我猜我肯定弄丢了一件，因为这是我剩下的唯一一件了。

sentences.en: Yeah, they're collector's items now.
sentences.zh: 是的，它们现在是收藏品了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It is very sad, because I can – my – what is it – autistic tendencies or OCD can tell me that it is the same logo that is misaligned.
sentences.zh: 这很悲哀，因为我——我的——怎么说呢——自闭倾向或强迫症能告诉我，这个标志是对不齐的。

sentences.en: The left – or I guess Bryce's right side of the logo is slightly thinner than the left side of the logo.
sentences.zh: 左侧——或者我猜是 Bryce 标志的右侧比左侧稍微细一点。

sentences.en: So in – as one of the other painful things – so the painful things I did with Thrust was, one, deal with the version control.
sentences.zh: 所以作为另一件痛苦的事情——我用 Thrust 做过的痛苦的事情之一是，处理版本控制。

sentences.en: Well, two, revitalized the docs twice.
sentences.zh: 嗯，第二，两次重振文档。

sentences.en: And then three, I had to reconstruct this logo.
sentences.zh: 然后第三，我不得不重建这个标志。

sentences.en: And I don't remember if I eventually – I think I may have gotten, like, some form of source image from Jared.
sentences.zh: 我不记得我最终是否——我想我可能从 Jared 那里得到了一些源图像。

sentences.en: But I remember there was something where, like, the fonts or something were missing, and I ended up having to, like –
sentences.zh: 但我记得当时有些问题，比如字体什么的丢失了，我最终不得不——

sentences.en: like, I spent, like, a week on getting the remade logo a little bit more correct.
sentences.zh: 我花了一周时间让重做的标志更准确一点。

sentences.en: But then, you know what I realized the other day was, why didn't I fix it so that the Thrust part fits all the way in the box?
sentences.zh: 但后来，你知道我前几天意识到什么吗？为什么我没有把它修好，让 Thrust 部分完全放进盒子里？

sentences.en: Like, I got this S and this T out here.
sentences.zh: 你看，S 和 T 都在外面。

sentences.en: Like, even on the updated one, it's not all the way in there.
sentences.zh: 即使在更新的版本上，它也没有完全放进去。

sentences.en: So I'm so bummed at myself, because I don't think I can – I don't think I can push through another logo change.
sentences.zh: 所以我对自己很沮丧，因为我觉得我不能——我觉得我无法再进行一次标志更改了。

sentences.en: The real question is, I mean, Thrust has within the name of it a programming language, a.k.a.
sentences.zh: 真正的问题是，Thrust 的名字里包含了一门编程语言，也就是

sentences.en: RuSt.
sentences.zh: RuSt。

sentences.en: I mean, which is a fantastic transition point to what is the future of parallel programming, parallel algorithm libraries?
sentences.zh: 我是说，这是一个绝佳的过渡点，讨论并行编程、并行算法库的未来是什么？

sentences.en: I mean, if you could restart today knowing everything you know now.
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果你今天能重新开始，了解你现在所知道的一切。

sentences.en: I mean, back when you were in the genesis of what became Thrust, you didn't know about reductions.
sentences.zh: 我是说，回到你处于 Thrust 起源的时候，你还不知道归约（reductions）。

sentences.en: You grew into it.
sentences.zh: 你是后来才接触到的。

sentences.en: And it's like, looking back on it, it seems obvious that you would know that stuff, but you didn't at the time.
sentences.zh: 回顾过去，似乎显而易见你会知道那些东西，但你当时并不知道。

sentences.en: And that is so true of, like, so many things that they teach in not just computer science but mathematics.
sentences.zh: 这对于很多事情来说都是如此，不仅是计算机科学，还有数学。

sentences.en: It's like, they teach you the artifact, but they don't teach you the path to it.
sentences.zh: 就像，他们教你成品，但他们不教你通往成品的路径。

sentences.en: And the path is very nonlinear.
sentences.zh: 而这条路径是非常非线性的。

sentences.en: How would you, if you were starting today, like, redesign a Thrust library?
sentences.zh: 如果你今天重新开始，你会如何重新设计 Thrust 库？

sentences.en: Because you've mentioned a couple times that, you know, it's kind of messy, the internals, and you don't need to divulge anything about your current work.
sentences.zh: 因为你提到过几次，你知道，它的内部结构有点乱，你不需要透露任何关于你目前工作的内容。

sentences.en: But if you were doing Thrust 2.0, maybe with a better name, with a better implementation, what would you do?
sentences.zh: 但如果你在做 Thrust 2.0，也许用一个更好的名字，更好的实现，你会怎么做？

sentences.en: Would it be in Rust?
sentences.zh: 它会是用 Rust 写的吗？

sentences.en: Would it be in C++?
sentences.zh: 它会是用 C++ 写的吗？

sentences.en: Tell all.
sentences.zh: 全盘托出吧。

sentences.en: I know what I would do.
sentences.zh: 我知道我会怎么做。

sentences.en: There's not a language, there's no current language that I think is sufficient, unfortunately.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，我认为目前没有一种语言是足够的。

sentences.en: But there's sort of three things that a language would need to do something like Thrust or just, you know, GPU parallelism really well.
sentences.zh: 但语言需要做类似 Thrust 或只是，你知道，GPU 并行处理得非常好，有三件事。

sentences.en: One is asynchrony.
sentences.zh: 一是异步性。

sentences.en: Thrust just fails at asynchrony for various reasons.
sentences.zh: Thrust 由于各种原因在异步性上失败了。

sentences.en: But I'd start, you know, start with a model for asynchrony.
sentences.zh: 但我会从，你知道，从一个异步模型开始。

sentences.en: And heterogeneity is important, by which I mean you really have to care about the fact that you're targeting more than one machine, and they have different architectures.
sentences.zh: 异构性也很重要，我的意思是，你必须真正关心这样一个事实：你的目标不仅仅是一台机器，而且它们有不同的架构。

sentences.en: And the differences in the architectures matter.
sentences.zh: 架构的差异很重要。

sentences.en: Even CUDA doesn't really have a good way to deal with this, unfortunately.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，即使是 CUDA 也没有很好的方法来处理这个问题。

sentences.en: And I base it all around tensors, not one-dimensional sequences.
sentences.zh: 我会把它全部建立在张量（tensors）周围，而不是一维序列。

sentences.en: Tensors and multidimensionality is sort of really important for parallelism, and it's important for sort of vital to everything that people do with GPUs,
sentences.zh: 张量和多维性对于并行性非常重要，对于人们使用 GPU 所做的一切来说，它几乎是至关重要的，

sentences.en: maybe aside from video games.
sentences.zh: 也许电子游戏除外。

sentences.en: I don't know how much tensors are important for video games, but everything else you do with the GPU involves tensors in some way.
sentences.zh: 我不知道张量对电子游戏有多重要，但你用 GPU 做的其他一切都以某种方式涉及张量。

sentences.en: Even the implementation of Thrust today implicitly revolves around tensors, because you have these...
sentences.zh: 即使是今天的 Thrust 实现也隐含地围绕着张量，因为你有这些……

sentences.en: I'm pretty sure the video games are just like, you know, one out of every ten frame is real, and the other nine are AI.
sentences.zh: 我很确定电子游戏只是，你知道，每十帧里有一帧是真的，其他九帧是 AI。

sentences.en: So I think it's all just tensors these days.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为现在一切都是张量。

sentences.en: Yeah, I agree.
sentences.zh: 是的，我同意。

sentences.en: But I think a good language for doing GPU parallelism really well would have to tackle at least those three things.
sentences.zh: 但我认为一门能很好地处理 GPU 并行性的优秀语言至少必须解决这三件事。

sentences.en: And, you know, as I was saying, whenever you write a CUDA kernel, you're implicitly doing tensor stuff, because every GPU is sort of shaped like a tensor in the architecture.
sentences.zh: 而且，正如我所说，每当你编写 CUDA 内核时，你都在隐含地做张量处理，因为每个 GPU 在架构上都像一个张量。

sentences.en: So if you're doing something like a thrust reduce, whether you know it or not, when you take that input sequence,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你在做类似 thrust reduce 的事情，无论你是否意识到，当你获取那个输入序列时，

sentences.en: you have to sort of fold it into a shape that matches the shape of the hardware.
sentences.zh: 你必须以某种方式将其折叠成与硬件形状相匹配的形状。

sentences.en: And inevitably, that's some sort of multidimensional shape.
sentences.zh: 不可避免地，那是一种多维形状。

sentences.en: So having a language where that was more explicit and can be taken advantage of would be really valuable for implementing libraries like ThruSt.
sentences.zh: 所以拥有一种能更明确地利用这一点的语言，对于实现像 Thrust 这样的库将非常有价值。

sentences.en: So those are some things I would do differently.
sentences.zh: 所以这些是我会做出的不同之处。

sentences.en: I mean, there's a whole lot of problems with Thrust that are there because for C++ reasons.
sentences.zh: 我是说，Thrust 存在很多问题，是因为 C++ 的原因。

sentences.en: And, you know, people have various different opinions on how to solve C++ problems, but really a better language would be better to work with.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，人们对如何解决 C++ 问题有各种不同的看法，但实际上，一门更好的语言会更好用。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, Rust is not that language.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，Rust 并不是那门语言。

sentences.en: Rust, I write in Rust every day.
sentences.zh: Rust，我每天都用 Rust 编写代码。

sentences.en: I really like it.
sentences.zh: 我真的很喜欢它。

sentences.en: It's good for single-threaded code, but I don't think it handles parallelism that well.
sentences.zh: 它对单线程代码很好，但我不认为它能很好地处理并行性。

sentences.en: And I don't think it knows what to do with GPU parallelism at all.
sentences.zh: 而且我不认为它知道该如何处理 GPU 并行性。

sentences.en: It's sort of at odds with GPU parallelism, unfortunately.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，它与 GPU 并行性有点格格不入。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有趣。

sentences.en: Like the way that borrow checking works sort of assumes that you've got a single thread and it's going to call functions in sequential order.
sentences.zh: 借用检查（borrow checking）的工作方式假设你有一个单线程，并且它将按顺序调用函数。

sentences.en: And the borrow checker works really well when you're doing that.
sentences.zh: 当你这样做时，借用检查器工作得非常好。

sentences.en: But on a GPU, we have a group of threads and they want to communicate and maybe they want to mutate different parts of a shared array.
sentences.zh: 但在 GPU 上，我们有一组线程，它们想要通信，也许它们想要改变共享数组的不同部分。

sentences.en: And no one knows how to make that work with borrow checking.
sentences.zh: 没有人知道如何让它与借用检查协同工作。

sentences.en: But what if you don't program the threads and the parallelism directly?
sentences.zh: 但如果不是直接对线程和并行进行编程呢？

sentences.en: What if the way that you express the parallelism is by performing operations on arrays that get paralyzed?
sentences.zh: 如果表达并行的方式是通过对数组执行操作，而这些操作会自动并行化呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, so what if you just threw out mutation?
sentences.zh: 没错，那如果直接抛弃可变性（mutation）呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's the other way to do it, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，那是另一种实现方式，没错。

sentences.en: Let's just not mutate the data or let's let the compiler decide how to parallelize collective operations on tensors or something like that.
sentences.zh: 我们干脆不要去修改数据，或者让编译器来决定如何对张量等对象上的集合操作进行并行化。

sentences.en: But that's great.
sentences.zh: 但这很棒。

sentences.en: You don't need Rust for that.
sentences.zh: 你不需要为此使用 Rust。

sentences.en: I mean, it's sort of Rust assumes you're going to mutate very carefully and you're going to think very carefully about sharing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，Rust 在某种程度上假设你会非常小心地进行修改，并且会非常仔细地考虑共享问题。

sentences.en: But if there's no sharing and there's no mutation, you don't need a borrow checker at all.
sentences.zh: 但如果没有共享，也没有可变性，你根本就不需要借用检查器（borrow checker）。

sentences.en: Ah, that's an interesting point.
sentences.zh: 啊，这是一个有趣的观点。

sentences.en: That's a very interesting point.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常有趣的观点。

sentences.en: I had not considered that.
sentences.zh: 我之前没考虑过这一点。

sentences.en: That if you're in a purely value-based world, like, why use Rust?
sentences.zh: 即如果你处于一个纯粹基于值的世界里，为什么还要用 Rust 呢？

sentences.en: Why not just, there's like dozens of options for that, yeah.
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？反正有几十种选择，没错。

sentences.en: Well, we've got armies of people working on different MLYR dialects, right?
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们有大批的人在研究不同的 MLIR 方言，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So we need to leverage those armies in a way that makes sense in a high-level language.
sentences.zh: 所以我们需要以一种在高级语言中合理的方式来利用这些人力。

sentences.en: At least that's my opinion.
sentences.zh: 至少我是这么认为的。

sentences.en: And I would definitely start with just value semantics.
sentences.zh: 我绝对会从值语义（value semantics）开始。

sentences.en: Just not necessarily functional, but like SSA sort of semantics.
sentences.zh: 不一定非要是函数式的，但类似于 SSA（静态单赋值）那样的语义。

sentences.en: That's what MLYR gives you anyway.
sentences.zh: 反正 MLIR 给你的就是这些。

sentences.en: I think you can get really far with that, especially for the kinds of algorithms that are in ThruSt.
sentences.zh: 我认为你可以用它走得很远，尤其是对于 Thrust 中那种类型的算法。

sentences.en: If you sort of assume that you have at your disposal operations that might look similar to what you would see in Cub,
sentences.zh: 如果你假设自己可以随意使用那些看起来类似于你在 Cub 中看到的操作，

sentences.en: but they're sort of, instead of mutating arrays in shared memory, you're instead just performing collective operations on values.
sentences.zh: 但它们不是在共享内存中修改数组，而是对值执行集合操作。

sentences.en: You could easily build a Thrust library or a Thrust-like algorithms like that.
sentences.zh: 你可以很容易地构建一个 Thrust 库或类似的算法库。

sentences.en: You just need a language to express it in.
sentences.zh: 你只需要一种语言来表达它。

sentences.en: I guess another thing we need, one really bad thing about libraries like Thrust or Cub or Cutlass is that they are locked in CUDA C++ templates, right?
sentences.zh: 我想我们还需要另一件事，像 Thrust、Cub 或 Cutlass 这样的库有一个非常糟糕的地方，就是它们被锁定在 CUDA C++ 模板中，对吧？

sentences.en: So to get access to them and reuse those implementations, you need to generate C++ code, and then you need to find a C++ compiler to instantiate that code.
sentences.zh: 所以要访问它们并重用这些实现，你需要生成 C++ 代码，然后你需要找一个 C++ 编译器来实例化这些代码。

sentences.en: Like, think about what we do from, you know, Python libraries that want to use the GPU.
sentences.zh: 比如，想想我们从那些想要使用 GPU 的 Python 库中所做的事情。

sentences.en: Inevitably, they generate some C++ code at runtime, compile it, and execute it.
sentences.zh: 不可避免地，它们会在运行时生成一些 C++ 代码，编译它，然后执行它。

sentences.en: But what if, you know, they didn't have to do that?
sentences.zh: 但如果它们不必这样做呢？

sentences.en: But what if those implementations were in a more portable form than C++ templates?
sentences.zh: 如果这些实现以一种比 C++ 模板更具可移植性的形式存在呢？

sentences.en: What if you didn't need a C++ compiler to use to get access to fast algorithms like you're in Cub, for example?
sentences.zh: 如果你不需要 C++ 编译器就能访问像 Cub 中那样的快速算法，那会怎样？

sentences.en: That's something we need.
sentences.zh: 这是我们需要的东西。

sentences.en: So I guess the question is, what is preventing us from having the world that you are describing right now today?
sentences.zh: 所以我猜问题在于，是什么阻碍了我们拥有你现在描述的那个世界？

sentences.en: Obviously, Python, I think the three of us in this meeting can agree.
sentences.zh: 显然是 Python，我想我们会议中的三个人都能达成共识。

sentences.en: And the folks that have the prerequisite knowledge to also agree with us can agree that Python is the non-ideal language for targeting GPUs.
sentences.zh: 而且那些具备必要知识的人也会同意我们的观点，即 Python 并不是针对 GPU 编程的理想语言。

sentences.en: It's dynamic.
sentences.zh: 它是动态的。

sentences.en: Oh, no, I think, I think, I think, I'll take a contrary perspective here.
sentences.zh: 哦不，我想，我想，我想，我要持相反的观点。

sentences.en: I think Python's great.
sentences.zh: 我认为 Python 很棒。

sentences.en: I made this, I was, for the first time ever, I've been on another podcast, the Talk Python to Me podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我做过这个，我当时是第一次参加另一个播客，Talk Python to Me 播客。

sentences.en: And I made this point that I will claim that Python is actually a performance-oriented language.
sentences.zh: 我提出了一个观点，我声称 Python 实际上是一种面向性能的语言。

sentences.en: And the reason for this is that Python has very loosey-goosey semantics.
sentences.zh: 原因在于 Python 拥有非常宽松的语义。

sentences.en: It's a very flexible language.
sentences.zh: 它是一种非常灵活的语言。

sentences.en: And it does not have a ton of rigorous protocol when interfacing with other languages.
sentences.zh: 而且在与其他语言交互时，它没有那么多严格的协议。

sentences.en: And it's very easy to build a DSL in Python.
sentences.zh: 在 Python 中构建 DSL（领域特定语言）非常容易。

sentences.en: It's very easy to build something that takes Python syntax and kind of Python semantics and lower it down to native code.
sentences.zh: 构建一个获取 Python 语法和某种 Python 语义并将其降低（lower）为原生代码的东西非常容易。

sentences.en: And it's also very easy for Python to call into native code.
sentences.zh: 而且 Python 调用原生代码也非常容易。

sentences.en: I remember a few years ago, I went to this, like, conference at Facebook.
sentences.zh: 我记得几年前，我去参加了 Facebook 的一个会议。

sentences.en: This was back when I was in California.
sentences.zh: 那是我还在加州的时候。

sentences.en: And there was this fellow who was a very senior, like, JVM engineer.
sentences.zh: 当时有一个人，他是一位非常资深的 JVM 工程师。

sentences.en: And he was talking about, he gave, like, a 30-minute talk solely on all the work that they had to do to make JVM native calls faSt.
sentences.zh: 他做了一个 30 分钟的演讲，专门讲他们为了让 JVM 原生调用变快所做的工作。

sentences.en: And the reason that they had to do all this work, it was, like, the calling convention for JVM to call native code was, like,
sentences.zh: 他们之所以必须做所有这些工作，是因为 JVM 调用原生代码的调用约定，

sentences.en: at minimum 100 instructions because the JVM had these very, very specific, you know, protocols for, like, you know, relating to, like, object semantics.
sentences.zh: 至少需要 100 条指令，因为 JVM 有非常、非常具体的协议，你知道的，与对象语义相关。

sentences.en: And you had to follow all these rules.
sentences.zh: 你必须遵循所有这些规则。

sentences.en: Whereas, like, in Python, it can just be, like, oh, you just call this function.
sentences.zh: 然而在 Python 中，它可能只是，哦，你直接调用这个函数就行了。

sentences.en: You just call this function, you know.
sentences.zh: 你直接调用这个函数，你知道的。

sentences.en: And, like, yeah, maybe, like, if you want to have, like, two-way interop, like, maybe the function needs to, like, use some of the Python APIs.
sentences.zh: 而且，是的，也许如果你想进行双向互操作，函数可能需要使用一些 Python API。

sentences.en: But, like, it's super simple in Python to just call a C function.
sentences.zh: 但用 Python 调用 C 函数超级简单。

sentences.en: And that makes it easy for Python to call into fast things.
sentences.zh: 这使得 Python 很容易调用快速的东西。

sentences.en: And then also on top of that, it's easy to extend to Python to build DSLs for Python.
sentences.zh: 而且除此之外，扩展 Python 以构建 Python 的 DSL 也很容易。

sentences.en: And so because of that, I think of Python as being more a performance-oriented language.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，我认为 Python 更像是一种面向性能的语言。

sentences.en: I think Python's more similar to C++ and Rust in that it is used, I would say, maybe not predominantly,
sentences.zh: 我认为 Python 与 C++ 和 Rust 更相似，因为它被使用，我想说，也许不是主要地，

sentences.en: but certainly it's getting closer and closer to that point where Python is predominantly used for performance-oriented tasks like machine learning and data science.
sentences.zh: 但可以肯定的是，它正越来越接近这一点，即 Python 主要用于机器学习和数据科学等面向性能的任务。

sentences.en: I've heard you say this three times now, that Python is performance-oriented.
sentences.zh: 我已经听到你说了三次了，说 Python 是面向性能的。

sentences.en: And I literally thought the first time you said it, I was going to be like, oh, he said it one time.
sentences.zh: 我第一次听到时真的想说，哦，他只说了一次。

sentences.en: I won't be able to call him out on it.
sentences.zh: 我没法反驳他。

sentences.en: You said that three times.
sentences.zh: 你说了三次了。

sentences.en: Are you serious?
sentences.zh: 你是认真的吗？

sentences.en: I am serious.
sentences.zh: 我是认真的。

sentences.en: Hey, we have free threading now.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我们现在有自由线程（free threading）了。

sentences.en: It's all going to be faSt.
sentences.zh: 一切都会变快的。

sentences.en: It's going to be very faSt.
sentences.zh: 会变得非常快。

sentences.en: Jared, can you back me up?
sentences.zh: Jared，你能支持我吗？

sentences.en: What are we talking about here?
sentences.zh: 我们到底在说什么？

sentences.en: A non-compiled, dynamic, interpreted language that treats integers as objects?
sentences.zh: 一种将整数视为对象的非编译、动态、解释型语言？

sentences.en: What are we talking about here, Bryce?
sentences.zh: Bryce，我们到底在说什么？

sentences.en: What are we talking about here?
sentences.zh: 我们到底在说什么？

sentences.en: But the point is that in the places where you care about performance, you can use a JIT.
sentences.zh: 但重点是，在你在意性能的地方，你可以使用 JIT（即时编译器）。

sentences.en: Like, if you write...
sentences.zh: 比如，如果你写……

sentences.en: Wait, wait, wait.
sentences.zh: 等等，等等，等等。

sentences.en: You just said it was performance-oriented.
sentences.zh: 你刚才说它是面向性能的。

sentences.en: And now you're saying in the places where you care you can use it?
sentences.zh: 现在你又说在你在意的地方可以使用它？

sentences.en: It treats integers as opt in the base language.
sentences.zh: 它在基础语言中把整数视为对象。

sentences.en: Like, if you want performance, it's better to use NumPy instead of the baked-in lists to Python.
sentences.zh: 比如，如果你想要性能，最好使用 NumPy 而不是 Python 内置的列表。

sentences.en: Like, as soon as you're over 1,000...
sentences.zh: 比如，一旦你超过 1000 个……

sentences.en: Not if you're using JIT?
sentences.zh: 如果你使用 JIT 呢？

sentences.en: What do you mean JIT?
sentences.zh: 你说的 JIT 是什么意思？

sentences.en: One second, one second.
sentences.zh: 等一下，等一下。

sentences.en: I'm pulling up some...
sentences.zh: 我正在调出一些……

sentences.en: The reason Bryce can say this is because Python is backed by Google and has been for the past 20 years.
sentences.zh: Bryce 能这么说的原因是，Python 有 Google 支持，而且过去 20 年一直如此。

sentences.en: And Google is the ones that have been paying to make all of these libraries fast through Python, right?
sentences.zh: 而 Google 一直在花钱通过 Python 让所有这些库变快，对吧？

sentences.en: But as soon as you need to do something that one of these libraries doesn't have a C API for, you're screwed, right?
sentences.zh: 但一旦你需要做一些这些库没有 C API 的事情，你就完蛋了，对吧？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That is true.
sentences.zh: 那是真的。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that's the thing is that, like, in general, if you...
sentences.zh: 这就是问题所在，通常情况下，如果你……

sentences.en: I've said this before on the podcast that, like, if you want performance code in Python, you shouldn't use Python.
sentences.zh: 我之前在播客上说过，如果你想要 Python 中的高性能代码，你不应该使用 Python。

sentences.en: You should use NumPy because NumPy is implemented in C, and as soon as you're doing anything serious, and by serious, I mean greater than 1,000 elements in a list,
sentences.zh: 你应该使用 NumPy，因为 NumPy 是用 C 实现的，一旦你做任何严肃的事情，我所说的严肃是指列表中超过 1000 个元素，

sentences.en: it's faster just in any library that's dispatching to C code, which means, how is Python performance-oriented?
sentences.zh: 任何分发到 C 代码的库都会更快，这意味着，Python 怎么就面向性能了？

sentences.en: That means that Python is a language that facilitates fast libraries that are not actually in Python.
sentences.zh: 这意味着 Python 是一种促进快速库的语言，而这些库实际上并不是用 Python 写的。

sentences.en: Yes, that is true, but also Python has a number of different JIT options that are very good.
sentences.zh: 是的，那是真的，但 Python 也有许多非常好的 JIT 选项。

sentences.en: So this is, like, we use NumPy as the basis of our, like, Cuda Python device code authoring.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们使用 NumPy 作为我们编写 Cuda Python 设备代码的基础。

sentences.en: And so you can write kernels in Cuda Python that will compile down to the same machine code that you would get if you wrote them in Cuda C++.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以用 Cuda Python 编写内核，它会编译成与你用 Cuda C++ 编写时相同的机器码。

sentences.en: And you can use abstractions like lists.
sentences.zh: 而且你可以在这段代码中使用列表这样的抽象。

sentences.en: Like, you can use all the Pythonic things in this code because it's just this, like, little DSL that is...
sentences.zh: 比如，你可以在这段代码中使用所有 Python 的东西，因为它只是这个小小的 DSL，它是……

sentences.en: NumPy's going to kind of violate some of the object semantics.
sentences.zh: NumPy 会违反一些对象语义。

sentences.en: You're not going to have an interpreter.
sentences.zh: 你不会有解释器。

sentences.en: You're not going to have object lifetimes.
sentences.zh: 你不会有对象生命周期。

sentences.en: It's going to map everything down to value semantic things in the C++ machine model, and you'll get the same perf.
sentences.zh: 它会将一切映射到 C++ 机器模型中的值语义事物，你会得到相同的性能。

sentences.en: And now you can even use our device-side libraries in something like NumPyCuda.
sentences.zh: 现在你甚至可以在 NumPyCuda 之类的东西中使用我们的设备端库。

sentences.en: So, like, yeah, like, Python, like, on its face is, like, you know, can be pretty slow.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，Python 从表面上看，你知道，可能相当慢。

sentences.en: But Python gives you all the tools to make it very, very faSt.
sentences.zh: 但 Python 给了你所有让它变得非常、非常快的工具。

sentences.en: Right, so are you talking about publicly about how it works?
sentences.zh: 对，所以你在公开谈论它是如何工作的吗？

sentences.en: Or is that not publicly not known?
sentences.zh: 还是说这不为人知？

sentences.en: No, it's all open source.
sentences.zh: 不，这都是开源的。

sentences.en: It's all open source because Numba is just an open source JIT compiler.
sentences.zh: 这都是开源的，因为 Numba 只是一个开源的 JIT 编译器。

sentences.en: So, what Numba does is it just takes either Python bytecode or AST, and then it lowers it down to this IR called Numba IR.
sentences.zh: 所以，Numba 所做的是获取 Python 字节码或 AST，然后将其降低为一种称为 Numba IR 的中间表示。

sentences.en: And then all that Numba IR is used for is to do type inference, to figure out, hey, you're calling this function here.
sentences.zh: 然后所有这些 Numba IR 都用于进行类型推断，以弄清楚，嘿，你在这里调用了这个函数。

sentences.en: You know, what are all the types?
sentences.zh: 你知道，所有的类型是什么？

sentences.en: And then once you have all the types resolved, you lower it down to either LVM IR or MLIR.
sentences.zh: 一旦你解析了所有类型，你就会将其降低为 LLVM IR 或 MLIR。

sentences.en: And then it compiles just like it would native code.
sentences.zh: 然后它就像原生代码一样编译。

sentences.en: And there's, like, two or three, like, major JIT solutions like this for Python.
sentences.zh: Python 有两三个像这样主要的 JIT 解决方案。

sentences.en: And, you know, the best analogy I can give is, like, JavaScript.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我能给出的最好的类比就是 JavaScript。

sentences.en: So, JavaScript is another language which JITs very, very well.
sentences.zh: 所以，JavaScript 是另一种 JIT 效果非常好的语言。

sentences.en: You can write code in JavaScript, which, like, after it's been JIT, has performance that is close to the performance of native code.
sentences.zh: 你可以用 JavaScript 编写代码，在 JIT 编译后，其性能接近原生代码的性能。

sentences.en: You can't do that with a language like Java, which has a very rigorous object model that makes it very challenging to really be able to do that.
sentences.zh: 你不能用 Java 那样的语言做到这一点，因为它有一个非常严格的对象模型，使得实现这一点非常具有挑战性。

sentences.en: But with languages like JavaScript and Python, their object models are a really good fit.
sentences.zh: 但对于 JavaScript 和 Python 这样的语言，它们的对象模型非常契合。

sentences.en: And in particular, if you're writing lists like NumPy type code, like, Numba, when it lowers things down, if it sees lists, lists get lowered down to, you know, just like a,
sentences.zh: 特别是如果你在编写 NumPy 类型的代码，比如 Numba，当它降低事物时，如果它看到列表，列表会被降低为，你知道，就像一个，

sentences.en: you know, an aggregate type, the equivalent of, like, a std tuple.
sentences.zh: 你知道，一个聚合类型，相当于 std tuple。

sentences.en: You know, integers, floats, et cetera, when they get JIT compiled, they're just going to be lowered down to the equivalent, you know, native processor types.
sentences.zh: 你知道，整数、浮点数等，当它们被 JIT 编译时，它们会被降低为等效的、你知道，原生处理器类型。

sentences.en: And something like a NumPy array is just going to be lowered down to, like, a pointer plus some metadata, you know, the equivalent of, like, an mdspan.
sentences.zh: 而像 NumPy 数组这样的东西会被降低为，比如，一个指针加上一些元数据，你知道，相当于 mdspan。

sentences.en: But, yeah, like, Numba, it just goes, takes your DSL, takes your Python AST or your Python bytecode, turns it into this intermediate IR, and it does the typing,
sentences.zh: 但，是的，Numba，它只是获取你的 DSL，获取你的 Python AST 或 Python 字节码，将其转化为这种中间 IR，并进行类型化，

sentences.en: and then it becomes LVM IR or MLIR.
sentences.zh: 然后它就变成了 LLVM IR 或 MLIR。

sentences.en: And Numba is, like, the heaviest weight of the Python DSL compilers.
sentences.zh: Numba 是 Python DSL 编译器中最重量级的。

sentences.en: There's also a lot of other DSL compilers.
sentences.zh: 还有很多其他的 DSL 编译器。

sentences.en: There's some that do transpilation, so they take Python code, they turn it into C++.
sentences.zh: 有些做转译（transpilation），所以它们获取 Python 代码，将其转化为 C++。

sentences.en: This is actually what Kupy does.
sentences.zh: 这实际上就是 Kupy 所做的。

sentences.en: Kupy takes your Python code, and it turns it into, like, it'll spit out, like, Thrust or Cub code, and then it'll JIT compile that code.
sentences.zh: Kupy 获取你的 Python 代码，并将其转化为，比如，它会吐出 Thrust 或 Cub 代码，然后它会 JIT 编译该代码。

sentences.en: And then there's other compilers that will use an approach called tracing, where instead of, like, parsing the Python AST, they essentially just inject mock objects into your code.
sentences.zh: 还有其他编译器会使用一种称为追踪（tracing）的方法，它们不是解析 Python AST，而是本质上将模拟对象注入到你的代码中。

sentences.en: And then as your code executes, instead of doing whatever your code was supposed to do, it captures a trace, and it builds up, like, from your actual code execution,
sentences.zh: 然后当你的代码执行时，它不会执行你代码本应做的任何事情，而是捕获一个追踪，并从你的实际代码执行中构建，

sentences.en: it builds up a representation of your program.
sentences.zh: 它构建了你程序的表示。

sentences.en: And then they transform that, and they lower it down in whatever way.
sentences.zh: 然后它们转换该表示，并以任何方式将其降低。

sentences.en: This is how, like, things like Triton used to work, although I think they now have a more proper compiler framework.
sentences.zh: 这就是像 Triton 这样的东西过去的工作方式，尽管我认为它们现在有了更正规的编译器框架。

sentences.en: But there's a ton of these different, like, tracing frameworks.
sentences.zh: 但有大量的这些不同的追踪框架。

sentences.en: Like, one problem that we have at NVIDIA is that it's so easy to make DSLs in Python that we have, like, 20 DSLs in Python.
sentences.zh: 比如，我们在 NVIDIA 面临的一个问题是，在 Python 中制作 DSL 太容易了，以至于我们有 20 个 Python DSL。

sentences.en: Like, every two to three weeks, somebody's creating a new Python DSL.
sentences.zh: 比如，每两三周，就有人在创建一个新的 Python DSL。

sentences.en: Yeah, but what if you need to write a kernel?
sentences.zh: 是的，但如果你需要写一个内核呢？

sentences.en: Like, none of these approaches have anything to offer.
sentences.zh: 这些方法中没有一个能提供任何帮助。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, they do.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，它们可以。

sentences.en: You can totally write kernels in...
sentences.zh: 你完全可以用……来编写内核。

sentences.en: You can't write kernels really in Python.
sentences.zh: 你其实没法用 Python 编写内核。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, you have access to all the tools that you have and access to...
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊，你确实能用到你手头所有的工具，也能用到……

sentences.en: No one's serious as writing kernels in Python.
sentences.zh: 没人会真的用 Python 去写内核。

sentences.en: I'm telling you...
sentences.zh: 我跟你说……

sentences.en: Then why isn't Thrust written in Python?
sentences.zh: 那为什么 Thrust 不是用 Python 写的呢？

sentences.en: We could get there.
sentences.zh: 我们以后可能会做到。

sentences.en: So, like, this is like a speed of light softmax kernel written in, like, native Python.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就像是一个用原生 Python 编写的、达到光速的 Softmax 内核。

sentences.en: Python, you can allocate showed memory, you can allocate register memory, you can use cub, you can use, like, other libraries, too.
sentences.zh: 在 Python 里，你可以分配共享内存，可以分配寄存器内存，可以使用 CUB，还可以使用其他库。

sentences.en: Like, people are starting to use this.
sentences.zh: 你看，人们已经开始用这个了。

sentences.en: People are starting to write, like, serious kernels in Python.
sentences.zh: 人们已经开始用 Python 编写真正的内核了。

sentences.en: Why is it good for a kernel to look like that?
sentences.zh: 为什么内核写成那样会比较好？

sentences.en: Because, one, you get to do...
sentences.zh: 因为首先，你可以……

sentences.en: You get to use NumPy style arrays.
sentences.zh: 你可以使用 NumPy 风格的数组。

sentences.en: Like, Python has, like, de facto, very nice...
sentences.zh: Python 有一种事实上的、非常好的……

sentences.en: Ranked polymorphism.
sentences.zh: 秩多态性（Ranked polymorphism）。

sentences.en: Would you care to elaborate on that, sir?
sentences.zh: 先生，您愿意详细解释一下吗？

sentences.en: You're saying NumPy-like arrays, but the word is ranked polymorphism.
sentences.zh: 您提到了 NumPy 风格的数组，但那个词是“秩多态性”。

sentences.en: Like, that's the thing that Jared was saying, is if he was going to do it over again, he would implement it in terms of tensors.
sentences.zh: 就像 Jared 说的，如果让他重来一次，他会用张量（Tensor）的概念来实现它。

sentences.en: When you're implementing something in terms of tensors, it means if you have a two-dimensional or three-dimensional array, you don't have to spell map, map,
sentences.zh: 当你用张量的概念来实现某些东西时，这意味着如果你有一个二维或三维数组，你就不必反复写 map、map、

sentences.en: map in order to do an element-wise operation over your arbitrarily ranked array.
sentences.zh: map 来对任意秩的数组执行逐元素操作。

sentences.en: NumPy semantics is array language semantics.
sentences.zh: NumPy 语义就是数组语言的语义。

sentences.en: It means that if you want to do some element-wise operation, it's just a single character plus a scalar or something like that.
sentences.zh: 这意味着如果你想执行某种逐元素操作，只需要一个加号加上一个标量之类的就可以了。

sentences.en: So, like, that is one of the benefits of NumPy, which is a poorly implemented array language, is ranked polymorphism or broadcasting.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是 NumPy 的优势之一——尽管它是一个实现得很差的数组语言——那就是秩多态性或广播机制。

sentences.en: And this isn't even to mention the very cool thing that we announced at GTC this year, which is Kutile, which is a new,
sentences.zh: 这还没提到我们在今年 GTC 上宣布的非常酷的东西，也就是 Kutile，这是一个全新的、

sentences.en: higher-level programming model for CUDA that's entirely array-based, where you don't explicitly program threads.
sentences.zh: 完全基于数组的 CUDA 高级编程模型，你不需要显式地对线程进行编程。

sentences.en: And, like, this is what the speed of light softmax looks like in Kutile.
sentences.zh: 这就是 Kutile 实现的光速 Softmax 的样子。

sentences.en: And, like, on the left, you're seeing the NumPy code, and on the right, you're seeing the Kutile code, and they're very close.
sentences.zh: 左边是你看到的 NumPy 代码，右边是 Kutile 代码，它们非常接近。

sentences.en: And it's usually taking advantage of the rank polymorphism that Connor's talking about.
sentences.zh: 而且它通常利用了 Connor 提到的秩多态性。

sentences.en: But to get to the question, why would you want to write a kernel from Python, well, there's a very simple answer to that question, which is, if you can write the kernel in Python,
sentences.zh: 但回到那个问题，为什么你想用 Python 写内核？答案很简单：如果你能用 Python 写内核，

sentences.en: then you don't have to deal with having to support both C++ and Python in your application.
sentences.zh: 那么你就不必在应用程序中同时维护 C++ 和 Python 了。

sentences.en: Then you don't have to deal with having a C++ build system, and it solves a bunch of packaging problems for you,
sentences.zh: 你也不必处理 C++ 构建系统，这还顺便解决了一堆打包问题，

sentences.en: because instead of having to build a Python extension or a shared library that Python loads, you can just ship, you know, Python source code, which is what most Python projects do.
sentences.zh: 因为你不需要构建 Python 扩展或 Python 加载的共享库，只需要分发 Python 源代码就行了，大多数 Python 项目都是这么做的。

sentences.en: So, like, it saves, like, a lot of headache that people have to be able to do things like Python in the language.
sentences.zh: 所以，这省去了很多麻烦，让人们能够用 Python 这种语言来做这些事。

sentences.en: Sure, I'm not here to defend C++, I'm just, like, defending the idea of an ideal, what is the platonic ideal of GPU programming language?
sentences.zh: 当然，我不是来为 C++ 辩护的，我只是在探讨一个理想，即 GPU 编程语言的柏拉图式理想是什么？

sentences.en: I wouldn't begin with Python, I guess is what I'm saying.
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，我不会从 Python 开始。

sentences.en: I understand people have, people like Python, and they have requirements to use Python.
sentences.zh: 我理解人们喜欢 Python，也有使用 Python 的需求。

sentences.en: I just like to imagine what the perfect GPU language would look like.
sentences.zh: 我只是喜欢构想完美的 GPU 语言会是什么样子。

sentences.en: I would agree, and the reason I would agree is that there are, well, I think that the NumPy ecosystem and its prevalence in Python is a huge improvement over C++, having these,
sentences.zh: 我同意，我同意的原因是，嗯，我认为 NumPy 生态系统及其在 Python 中的普及，相比 C++ 是一个巨大的进步，拥有这些……

sentences.en: like, rank polymorphic arrays that are, it's a vocabulary type.
sentences.zh: 秩多态数组，这是一种词汇类型。

sentences.en: It's not, like, part of the language, but it's in such wide usage that, like, every library that does anything with tensors supports the NumPy semantics, and that's great.
sentences.zh: 它不是语言的一部分，但应用如此广泛，以至于每个处理张量的库都支持 NumPy 语义，这很棒。

sentences.en: However, NumPy is a little bit old, 20, 30 years old, and it does have, like, a number of words to it.
sentences.zh: 然而，NumPy 有点老了，有二三十年了，它确实有一些包袱。

sentences.en: One of the things...
sentences.zh: 其中一点是……

sentences.en: Whoa, whoa, whoa, whoa, let's back up.
sentences.zh: 等等，等等，等等，我们先退一步。

sentences.en: Python is 30 years old, not NumPy.
sentences.zh: Python 有 30 年历史，NumPy 没有。

sentences.en: You're getting your languages and your libraries confused.
sentences.zh: 你把语言和库搞混了。

sentences.en: Python was created in 1993 or 94.
sentences.zh: Python 是在 1993 或 94 年创建的。

sentences.en: NumPy was not.
sentences.zh: NumPy 不是。

sentences.en: When was NumPy created?
sentences.zh: NumPy 是什么时候创建的？

sentences.en: NumPy, I think it became popular around 2010, and I agree completely with Jared.
sentences.zh: NumPy，我想它是在 2010 年左右流行起来的，我完全同意 Jared 的观点。

sentences.en: Like, if I'm designing a GPU language from scratch, I'm not starting anywhere close to Python.
sentences.zh: 如果我要从零开始设计一种 GPU 语言，我绝不会从 Python 入手。

sentences.en: The fact that Python has become the lingua franqua of...
sentences.zh: 事实上，Python 已经成为了……的通用语。

sentences.en: In 2005, by, yeah, Travis Oliphong, who is someone I hope to...
sentences.zh: 2005 年，由 Travis Oliphant，我希望……的人。

sentences.en: When was 2005?
sentences.zh: 2005 年是什么时候？

sentences.en: It was 20 years ago.
sentences.zh: 那是 20 年前。

sentences.en: I said 20 years.
sentences.zh: 我说的是 20 年。

sentences.en: That is 50...
No, no, no, you said 30.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不，你说的是 30。

sentences.en: 30 was the genesis of Python.
sentences.zh: 30 年是 Python 的起源。

sentences.en: I had dinner with...
sentences.zh: 我和……吃过晚饭。

sentences.en: We were at the same dinner table at the PyLadies charity auction with Travis Oliphong last week.
sentences.zh: 上周在 PyLadies 慈善拍卖会上，我们和 Travis Oliphant 同桌吃饭。

sentences.en: Very nice fellow.
sentences.zh: 非常棒的人。

sentences.en: Fantastic, fantastic.
sentences.zh: 太棒了，太棒了。

sentences.en: My point being is that I agree with Jared.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我同意 Jared 的观点。

sentences.en: Python was created 30 years ago, NumPy halfway through the lifetime of Python, and a dynamically quasi-strongly typed language with all this, you know, great, you know, FFI.
sentences.zh: Python 创建于 30 年前，NumPy 是在 Python 生命周期的中段出现的，它是一种动态的、准强类型的语言，拥有所有这些很棒的 FFI。

sentences.en: That's not...
sentences.zh: 那不是……

sentences.en: The reason that Python today is the language that folks use to target GPUs is not because it's a good language for targeting GPUs.
sentences.zh: 今天人们使用 Python 作为 GPU 编程语言，并不是因为它适合编写 GPU 程序。

sentences.en: It is okay, but it's not where I would start.
sentences.zh: 它还可以，但不是我会选择的起点。

sentences.en: And I think that's what Jared was trying to say, is that it...
sentences.zh: 我想这正是 Jared 想表达的，它……

sentences.en: I think Python gets in the way of what we would like from a language in terms of trying to eke out max efficiency and performance from GPUs.
sentences.zh: 我认为 Python 阻碍了我们对语言的期望，特别是在试图从 GPU 中榨取最大效率和性能时。

sentences.en: And it's just an artifact of history that it's become the lingua franca of data science and machine learning and deep learning, etc.
sentences.zh: 它成为数据科学、机器学习和深度学习的通用语，纯粹是历史的偶然。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Maybe, Jared, you could add if you disagree with what I just said.
sentences.zh: 也许 Jared 你可以补充一下，如果你不同意我刚才说的话。

sentences.en: So I picked up Python recently because I was considering using it for a project.
sentences.zh: 我最近开始接触 Python，因为我考虑在一个项目中使用它。

sentences.en: And whenever I use Python, I feel like I've loSt...
sentences.zh: 每当我使用 Python 时，我就感觉我失去了……

sentences.en: Like I've gone blind.
sentences.zh: 就像我瞎了一样。

sentences.en: Like I've lost a sense because there are no types.
sentences.zh: 就像我失去了一种感官，因为没有类型。

sentences.en: And even when there are types, they're not really there, right?
sentences.zh: 即使有类型，它们也不是真的存在，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, they don't do anything for you.
sentences.zh: 它们对你没有任何帮助。

sentences.en: So I feel like...
sentences.zh: 所以我感觉……

sentences.en: I mean, even if you use the type ascriptions, they don't...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，即使你使用了类型标注，它们也不……

sentences.en: They're not helpful.
sentences.zh: 它们没什么用。

sentences.en: So I don't know.
sentences.zh: 所以我不知道。

sentences.en: I just feel like I have brain damage or something when I'm reading or writing Python code.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得在阅读或编写 Python 代码时，我的大脑好像受损了。

sentences.en: I like Rust because once CargoCheck is happy with the program, I'm confident it's going to work.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢 Rust，因为一旦 CargoCheck 对程序满意，我就确信它能运行。

sentences.en: I can do enormous refactors to a code base and be confident that they were correct.
sentences.zh: 我可以对代码库进行大规模重构，并确信它们是正确的。

sentences.en: And nothing like that is possible with Python.
sentences.zh: 而 Python 根本做不到这一点。

sentences.en: I know it's important.
sentences.zh: 我知道它很重要。

sentences.en: I know it's probably the most important programming language.
sentences.zh: 我知道它可能是最重要的编程语言。

sentences.en: But there are some things that Python is inadequate for.
sentences.zh: 但 Python 在某些方面确实力不从心。

sentences.en: So there's a particular wart of NumPy that I want to highlight.
sentences.zh: NumPy 有一个特别的缺陷，我想强调一下。

sentences.en: But if I highlight that wart, it rapidly leads into the really cool algorithm that I want to show you.
sentences.zh: 但如果我强调那个缺陷，它很快就会引出我想向你们展示的那个非常酷的算法。

sentences.en: And I suspect that Connor may have a couple topics he wants to discuss with Jared before we get there.
sentences.zh: 我怀疑 Connor 在我们开始之前，可能还有几个话题想和 Jared 讨论。

sentences.en: No, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不。

sentences.en: I mean, we can go down this rabbit hole.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们可以深入探讨一下。

sentences.en: I would just like to go on record saying that Python is the most popular language in the world
sentences.zh: 我只想记录在案，Python 是世界上最流行的语言，

sentences.en: at the time that LLMs have come of age, which makes you think that the rich are just going to get richer.
sentences.zh: 在大语言模型（LLM）成熟的时代，这让你觉得富人只会越来越富。

sentences.en: I am willing to bet my life on the fact that Python will not be the actual language that LLMs target because it's not...
sentences.zh: 我敢拿我的生命打赌，Python 不会是 LLM 最终瞄准的语言，因为它不是……

sentences.en: A language like Rust that is statically typed, has more linting, etc., is better to target.
sentences.zh: 像 Rust 这样静态类型、有更多代码检查工具的语言，更适合作为目标。

sentences.en: Than a dynamically typed language.
sentences.zh: 比动态类型语言更好。

sentences.en: And so anyways, I'm just going on record saying Python is popular now and will die before I die.
sentences.zh: 总之，我只是记录在案，Python 现在很流行，但在我死之前它会消亡。

sentences.en: And that's also keeping in mind that I will upload my brain to the cloud and live forever.
sentences.zh: 当然，还要考虑到我会把我的大脑上传到云端并永生。

sentences.en: At which point we will now transition to Bryce's segue into his algorithm that he wants to talk about.
sentences.zh: 那么现在，我们转入 Bryce 的过渡环节，谈谈他想讲的算法。

sentences.en: So before we get there, a quick thing on LLMs.
sentences.zh: 在开始之前，先简单说一下 LLM。

sentences.en: So I've been thinking a little bit recently about this question about like what language will the LLMs write code in?
sentences.zh: 我最近一直在思考一个问题：LLM 会用什么语言编写代码？

sentences.en: And one thing that's come up is this question of coding conventions.
sentences.zh: 其中一个出现的问题是编码规范。

sentences.en: In particular, what coding conventions should we as programmers follow to make it easier to use LLMs in our code bases?
sentences.zh: 特别是，我们作为程序员应该遵循什么样的编码规范，才能让 LLM 更容易地使用我们的代码库？

sentences.en: And one particular piece of this that's come to mind to me has been around naming conventions.
sentences.zh: 其中一个引起我注意的方面是命名规范。

sentences.en: I think typically, at least me, I tend to prefer...
sentences.zh: 我想通常情况下，至少对我来说，我倾向于……

sentences.en: Early in my career, I would use very long and verbose names.
sentences.zh: 职业生涯早期，我喜欢使用非常长且冗长的名称。

sentences.en: But now, I primarily write code for slides.
sentences.zh: 但现在，我主要为幻灯片编写代码。

sentences.en: And I got a limited number of characters that I can use in the slide.
sentences.zh: 幻灯片里能用的字符数有限。

sentences.en: And so I found myself using shorter and shorter names as my career goes on.
sentences.zh: 所以随着职业生涯的发展，我发现自己使用的名称越来越短。

sentences.en: But it seems to me like you probably want to use quite descriptive names in your code base if you're planning on using LLMs to help you write your code.
sentences.zh: 但对我来说，如果你打算使用 LLM 来辅助编程，你可能还是希望在代码库中使用相当具有描述性的名称。

sentences.en: Maybe even you want to use names that are more verbose than would be comfortable for a human.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能比人类觉得舒适的名称还要冗长。

sentences.en: Because if you use very short names that could be ambiguous or misinterpreted, it might be more confusing to the LLM.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你使用非常短的名称，可能会产生歧义或被误解，这对 LLM 来说可能更令人困惑。

sentences.en: Whereas if you use very clear and concise names that are unambiguous, that's going to probably give you better results with using LLMs.
sentences.zh: 而如果你使用非常清晰、简洁且无歧义的名称，使用 LLM 时可能会得到更好的结果。

sentences.en: This is such a C++ programmer thing to worry about.
sentences.zh: 这真是典型的 C++ 程序员才会担心的事。

sentences.en: Because I used to worry about what to name things.
sentences.zh: 因为我过去也总是担心该怎么命名。

sentences.en: Because in C++, C++ is a very paranoid language.
sentences.zh: 因为在 C++ 中，C++ 是一门非常多疑的语言。

sentences.en: Because you have to think about all the things that can go wrong on any given line of code.
sentences.zh: 因为你必须考虑每一行代码中可能出错的所有情况。

sentences.en: Like you could call the wrong function.
sentences.zh: 比如你可能会调用错误的函数。

sentences.en: Or the type the thing gets instantiated with is we'll be missing something.
sentences.zh: 或者实例化该对象时缺少了某些东西。

sentences.en: Or we'll have the wrong thing in it.
sentences.zh: 或者里面有错误的东西。

sentences.en: And so you have to take this very defensive stance when writing any C++ code.
sentences.zh: 所以你在编写任何 C++ 代码时都必须采取这种非常防御性的姿态。

sentences.en: Now that I've been using Rust for a while now, I don't worry about these things at all.
sentences.zh: 现在我使用 Rust 一段时间了，我根本不用担心这些事情。

sentences.en: I don't worry about what to call things.
sentences.zh: 我不用担心该怎么命名。

sentences.en: I don't worry about how the code looks.
sentences.zh: 我不用担心代码看起来怎么样。

sentences.en: Because I can be confident that it works.
sentences.zh: 因为我可以确信它能运行。

sentences.en: These problems just don't exist in Rust, I guess is what I'm saying.
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，这些问题在 Rust 中根本不存在。

sentences.en: These things I used to get paranoid about in my C++ template codes.
sentences.zh: 这些是我过去在 C++ 模板代码中会感到多疑的事情。

sentences.en: There's usually only one right way to write the Rust function according to some LLM.
sentences.zh: 对于 LLM 来说，编写 Rust 函数通常只有一种正确的方法。

sentences.en: And if it compiles, then it's correct.
sentences.zh: 只要能编译通过，它就是正确的。

sentences.en: And you move on.
sentences.zh: 然后你就可以继续做别的事了。

sentences.en: These ambiguities just simply don't exiSt.
sentences.zh: 这些歧义根本不存在。

sentences.en: It's a very relaxing way to write code.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常轻松的编程方式。

sentences.en: And I can echo that.
sentences.zh: 我对此深有同感。

sentences.en: It's when you write Rust code, like I am more of an expert in C++ than I am in Rust by two orders of magnitude.
sentences.zh: 当你编写 Rust 代码时，我虽然在 C++ 方面的造诣比 Rust 深两个数量级。

sentences.en: Like I've written a couple thousand lines of RuSt.
sentences.zh: 我只写过几千行 Rust 代码。

sentences.en: That doesn't make me an expert.
sentences.zh: 这并不能让我成为专家。

sentences.en: But, like, I know the inner details of the special member functions and all this stuff.
sentences.zh: 但是，我了解特殊成员函数之类的内部细节。

sentences.en: And I have so much, like, cognitive weight in my brain when I program C++.
sentences.zh: 当我编写 C++ 时，我的大脑里有太多的认知负担。

sentences.en: And I'm like, oh, am I using an initializer list?
sentences.zh: 我会想，哦，我是在使用初始化列表吗？

sentences.en: Well, I've got a special set of rules for that.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我有一套特殊的规则来处理它。

sentences.en: And it's just like I have all these voices talking in my head when I program in C++.
sentences.zh: 当我用 C++ 编程时，就像脑子里有各种声音在说话。

sentences.en: When I go to Rust, I'm kind of just like, I don't really know what's happening here.
sentences.zh: 当我转到 Rust 时，我有点像，我不太清楚这里发生了什么。

sentences.en: But the compiler, like, holds your hand and is like, don't worry.
sentences.zh: 但编译器会牵着你的手说，别担心。

sentences.en: I'll be the expert.
sentences.zh: 我会是专家。

sentences.en: You just program the way you want to program.
sentences.zh: 你只管按你想的方式编程就行了。

sentences.en: And all I'm saying is the future of generated code targets a language like that.
sentences.zh: 我只想说，生成式代码的未来将以这样的语言为目标。

sentences.en: Not like C++ where you have a matrix of special member functions where depending on the subset that you implemented, you will get a certain other set generated.
sentences.zh: 不像 C++ 那样，你有一套特殊的成员函数矩阵，根据你实现的子集不同，会生成另一套特定的函数。

sentences.en: It's, anyway, so, I mean, and that's C++.
sentences.zh: 总之，我是说，这就是 C++。

sentences.en: You're trying to say that Python, a dynamically typed, et cetera, et cetera, language is going to be the, no.
sentences.zh: 你是想说 Python 这种动态类型语言等等，会成为……不，不可能。

sentences.en: It's in the short term, that's what's going to happen.
sentences.zh: 短期内，情况确实会是这样。

sentences.en: In the long term, the more compiler, upfront, static analysis guarantees that you can get, that's what's going to be the future, in my opinion.
sentences.zh: 但从长远来看，我认为未来属于那些能提供更多编译器预先静态分析保证的语言。

sentences.en: But Bryce has a story to tell us about some algorithm and potentially refuting everything we're saying here.
sentences.zh: 不过 Bryce 有个关于某种算法的故事要讲，可能会推翻我们刚才所说的一切。

sentences.en: So we'll let Bryce speak now and convince us.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在让 Bryce 发言，让他来说服我们。
